bing.message:
My shortlist offers three alternative complete setups; buy just one.

The Breville Barista Express Impress at Williams Sonoma, $649.95, is my recommendation if you want to learn espresso with assisted dosing and tamping while steaming milk manually. Its integrated grinder avoids a separate grinder purchase. You still adjust the grind, handle the portafilter and clean the steam wand after use. Two sequential morning drinks are a reasonable fit.

The Ninja Luxe Cafe Mini at Target, $449.99, is the stronger savings option. Assuming the standard US Mini package, its integrated grinding and assisted milk preparation suit a beginner's milk-drink routine. The Breville costs $199.96 more; that premium makes most sense if you value its espresso-focused workflow and room to develop your technique.

The Philips 3300 at Amazon.com, $530, is worth choosing if automated brewing matters most. Its exact milk-system variant is unclear in this truncated card, so I would not promise one-touch milk drinks. Automatic machines also require regular milk-system and brew-unit cleaning.

These completeness judgments assume standard US retail packages: espresso-suitable integrated grinders, brewing and milk-steaming capability, and the normal portafilter, baskets, tamping mechanism and milk vessel—or built-in equivalents. Accessories and voltage are not independently verified by these cards. No separate scale or upgraded tools are necessary to start. Each alternative fits the $800 equipment budget before tax and shipping.

Williams Sonoma is the named retailer on the Breville offer. Target and Amazon platform labels alone do not establish the individual seller or specific return terms. My confidence uses ordinary brand and retail reputation assumptions, not verified warranties or the cards' ratings.

You still handle the portafilter and clean the basket, milk vessel and steam system after use.

Two alternatives are worth considering individually:

• De'Longhi Magnifica Evo with Automatic Milk Frother at $749.99, listed by Best Buy: choose this if automatic bean-to-cup preparation matters enough to justify another $150 over the Ninja. It reduces hands-on preparation, but the milk system and brewing mechanism still need regular cleaning.
